messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into French, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE French line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
Et une louve qui de toutes les convoitises semblait chargée dans sa maigreur, et déjà faisait vivre de nombreux gens dans le désespoir,

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑French Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation | Status | |-------------|----------------------|----------------------|------------------|--------| | Ed | coordinating conjunction “and” | Et | “and” | OK | | una | indefinite article “a” (fem. sg.) | une | “a” | OK | | lupa | noun “she‑wolf” | louve | “she‑wolf” | OK | | che | relative pronoun “who” | qui | “who” | OK | | di | preposition “with” | de | “with” | OK | | tutte | quantifier “all” (fem. pl.) | toutes | “all” | OK | | brame | noun “cravings” | convoitises *(les convoitises)* | “cravings” | OK | | sembiava | verb “seemed” (imperfect) | semblait | “seemed” | OK | | carca | adjective “laden” | chargée | “laden” | OK | | ne | preposition “in” | dans | “in” | OK | | la | definite article (part of “la sua”) | — *(omitted)* | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | sua | possessive adjective “her” | sa | “her” | OK | | magrezza | noun “meagreness” | maigreur | “meagreness” | OK | | e | coordinating conjunction “and” | et | “and” | OK | | molte | quantifier “many” (fem. pl.) | nombreux | “many” | OK | | genti | noun “folk, people” | gens | “people” | OK | | fé | verb “had made” (causative) | faisait | “made / caused” | OK | | già | adverb “already” | déjà | “already” | OK | | viver | infinitive “to live” | vivre | “to live” | OK | | grame | noun “forlornness, grief” | désespoir *(le désespoir)* | “forlornness” | OK |
### Items to Note - **UNNECESSARY**: - **la** – French does not use an article before the possessive *sa*. - **les** – article added before *convoitises* (French requires a definite article). - **de** – article before *nombreux* (French quantifier construction). - **le** – article before *désespoir*. - **dans** – preposition inserted before *désespoir* (source provides no preposition).
- **MISSING / WRONG / GRAMMAR**: none.
All source words are represented in the French translation; the only issues are the extra French function words that are required by French grammar but have no counterpart in the Italian source.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only French script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final French text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- Line 51: - Original: et déjà faisait vivre de nombreux gens dans le désespoir, - Issue: none - Corrected: et déjà faisait vivre de nombreux gens dans le désespoir,
